intervals.note: The data were taken in two runs (Run I and Run II) separated by a major maintenance interruption; the array was first cooled down at the beginning of 2003 (0802.3439).
intervals.quote: CUORICINO data acquisition started in April 2003 and ended in June 2008

quantity.quote: CUORICINO is an array of 62 tellurium oxide (T eO2 ) bolometers with an active mass of 40.7 kg.
with a total exposure of 19.75 kg·y of 130 Te

name: CUORICINO
notes: CUORE (experiment:cuore) is its successor; the lineage row (CUORICINO as predecessor) lives on the CUORE record.
No source calls the CUORICINO team a named collaboration: the papers are signed by individual authors, so no collaboration record is written.
The 2005 PRL (hep-ex/0501034) and the 2008 PRC (0802.3439) report earlier partial data sets; the 2008 paper's limit (3.0e24 yr, 11.83 kg y) was superseded by the final 2.8e24 yr (19.75 kg y) result.

physics_goals.quote: CUORICINO was able to set a lower bound on the 130 Te 0νββ half-life of 2.8 × 10^24 years at 90% C.L.
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double beta decay of 130Te with TeO2 bolometers, a pilot for CUORE

summary.plain: A tower of 62 tellurium-oxide crystals chilled to about 10 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero in the Gran Sasso laboratory, listening for the heat of a neutrinoless double beta decay. It ran from 2003 to 2008 and was the pilot for CUORE.
summary.technical: CUORICINO: 13-plane tower of 62 TeO2 crystals (40.7 kg, natural Te) read by NTD thermistors, cooled to 8-10 mK in a dilution refrigerator at LNGS (about 3650 m.w.e.). Final result with 19.75 kg y of 130Te: T1/2(0vbb) > 2.8e24 yr (90 % C.L.), <m_ee> < 300-710 meV.
